paragraphs: Friend, here's what this chapter says to me. Gedaliah was warned about Ishmael, and he called the warning a lie (Jeremiah 40:14-16). Then Ishmael sat down and ate a meal with him, and got up and struck him down with the sword (Jeremiah 41:1-2). I think this one hurts, and it's a heavy chapter. It shows that a warning you brush off doesn't go away just because you didn't want to hear it.

Now look at what came after. Johanan and the commanders went and got the people back from Ishmael, and the captives rejoiced (Jeremiah 41:11-14). That was a real rescue. But then they stopped near Bethlehem, planning to go into Egypt, because they were afraid of the Chaldeans (Jeremiah 41:17-18). I think fear was steering that wagon, friend. I've been scared enough to make a plan before I asked anybody about it, and my plans smell like burnt dough.

So here's the big idea. Listen to the warnings God's Word gives you, even when they're inconvenient, and don't let fear do your planning. Being rescued is wonderful, but it's not the same as knowing where to go next. And this story is not over, so keep your oven warm and your ears open.
